newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian bourse '96 turnover rises 70 times.
newsitem.headline: Croatian bourse '96 turnover rises 70 times.

text.p: Zagreb's bourse took off for real in 1996, with its first surges and plunges and a record total turnover of just under one billion kuna -- more than 70 times that of the previous year.

According to final trading figures released on Friday, over 343 million German marks worth of stocks and government bonds was traded at the Zagreb Stock Exchange, in comparison with a mere 4.5 million marks in 1995.
Trading received a great boost in April, when the leading Croatian company, Pliva pharmaceuticals, was listed at the London Stock Exchange.
The monthly turnover jumped to over 16 million marks in April from one million in March.
The leading commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka followed suit in July.
Autumn saw the first bull run ever, with prices of most liquid stocks jumping, and the monthly turnover rising to over 46 million marks in October.
While secondary trading in stocks and government bonds recorded a dramatic rise, public auctions of state-owned firms fell to 23 million marks from over 61 million in 1995.
